value.query: How to embed V8 using isolates contexts handles garbage collection and compare engine boundary requirements with JavaScriptCore

content.text:
### Configure Isolate with Custom Startup Snapshot

Source: https://github.com/v8/v8.dev/blob/main/src/blog/custom-startup-snapshots.md

Initialize a new V8 isolate to use a custom startup snapshot. Contexts created within this isolate will be exact copies of the snapshot, providing immediate access to its defined functions.

```c++
v8::Isolate::CreateParams params;
params.snapshot_blob = snapshot_blob;
v8::Isolate* isolate = v8::Isolate::New(params);
```

--------------------------------

### Create Global Object Template and Context

Source: https://github.com/v8/v8.dev/blob/main/src/docs/embed.md

This snippet demonstrates creating a template for the global object and setting built-in global functions like 'log'. It then creates a new V8 context using this template, ensuring each processor has an isolated JavaScript environment.

```cpp
// Create a template for the global object and set the
// built-in global functions.
v8::Local<v8::ObjectTemplate> global = v8::ObjectTemplate::New(isolate);
global->Set(v8::String::NewFromUtf8(isolate, "log"),
            v8::FunctionTemplate::New(isolate, LogCallback));

// Each processor gets its own context so different processors
// do not affect each other.
v8::Persistent<v8::Context> context =
    v8::Context::New(isolate, nullptr, global);
```

### Hello world

Source: https://github.com/v8/v8.dev/blob/main/src/docs/embed.md

An isolate is a VM instance with its own heap. A local handle is a pointer to an object, necessary due to V8's garbage collector. A handle scope acts as a container for handles, allowing for their collective deletion. A context is an execution environment for separate JavaScript code within a single V8 instance, and must be explicitly specified.

--------------------------------

### About V8

Source: https://github.com/v8/v8.dev/blob/main/src/docs/index.md

V8 implements ECMAScript and WebAssembly, and runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux systems that use x64, IA-32, or ARM processors. V8 can be embedded into any C++ application. It compiles and executes JavaScript source code, handles memory allocation for objects, and garbage collects objects it no longer needs. V8’s stop-the-world, generational, accurate garbage collector is one of the keys to V8’s performance.

--------------------------------

### Handles and garbage collection

Source: https://github.com/v8/v8.dev/blob/main/src/docs/embed.md

A handle provides a reference to a JavaScript object's location in the heap. The V8 garbage collector reclaims memory used by objects that can no longer be accessed. When the garbage collector moves an object, it updates all handles referring to it with the object's new location. An object is considered garbage if it is inaccessible from JavaScript and has no handles referring to it.
